advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the bridge_sync docstring/env help: without REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC=1 bridge_sync is DISABLED (raises), it does not fall back to dry-run.
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:5: `` ``bridge_sync`` defaults to non-mutating dry-run behavior.``
src/rebar/mcp_server.py:151-152: `"Set to 1 to allow bridge_sync to perform live (mutating) Jira sync; " "otherwise bridge_sync uses dry-run behavior."`
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:95-96: `if not _gate_value(ctx.allow_jira_sync): raise ValueError("bridge sync is disabled; set REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC=1 to enable")`
_lib_ops.bridge_sync (src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:270-280) calls _bridge_run('sync', ...) with no profile/dry-run parameter; dry-run is a bridge_run/bridge_preview profile, not a sync mode.
advisory.finding: The new module docstring and REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC help text claim bridge_sync 'defaults to non-mutating dry-run behavior' / 'otherwise bridge_sync uses dry-run behavior', but the actual bridge_sync tool RAISES ValueError('bridge sync is disabled') when the gate is unset — it does not fall back to any dry-run mode.
scenarios: An operator reads the env-var help, assumes running bridge_sync without the flag will safely produce a dry-run plan, and instead gets a hard 'disabled' error — or wrongly believes an unguarded call is safe.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword to state bridge_sync (and bridge_run/pause/resume) are disabled unless REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC=1; reserve the 'dry-run default' language for bridge_run's profile='dry-run' / bridge_preview.

Comments have no non-human consumer, so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception (for non-executable instruction artifacts) does not apply.
